title: N3 · Unit 6

lessons.title: An arrangement and a personal choice
lessons.description: Read what was agreed at the café, and what Bao chose to check tonight.
lessons.canDo: Separate a decision from its pending execution

lessons.title: No need, and requested advice
lessons.description: Hear why a duplicate call is unnecessary, then divide the remaining work.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish reassurance from prohibition and firm advice

grammar.title: A decision is not its completed action
grammar.formation: Dictionary or ない verb + ことにする. ことにした/しました reports a decision. ことにしている describes a chosen continuing practice.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the decision/routine taught in N4 units 11/12. State who chooses and whether execution is pending. A decision made yesterday can concern work tonight; a past した does not prove that work is finished.
grammar.example: 今夜、字幕を確認することにしました。
grammar.translation: I decided to check the subtitles tonight.

examples.ja: {今夜|こんや}、{字幕|じまく}を{確認|かくにん}することにしました。
examples.en: I decided to check the subtitles tonight.

examples.ja: {記憶|きおく}だけに{頼|たよ}らないことにしました。
examples.en: I decided not to rely only on memory.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}の{後|あと}でメモを{見直|みなお}すことにしています。
examples.en: I make a practice of reviewing the note after meetings.

grammar.mistake: 行かないことにする decides not to go. 行くことにしない negates deciding to go and is not automatically the same decision. Do not mark a planned check as completed.

grammar.title: Report the arrangement and its grounds
grammar.formation: Dictionary or ない verb + ことになる. ことになった/なりました reports a decided arrangement or result; it can still be future. Attributive adjective + ことになる can express a resulting situation rather than an enacted decision.
grammar.explanation: Present what the discussion or circumstances have led to. Give the stated source of the arrangement: here the café team and the manager’s permission. ことになる can also indirectly present the speaker’s own choice, so identify the actor from the scene rather than treating it as a grammar-only external-agency rule.
grammar.example: 会議で、土曜日に映画を見ることになりました。
grammar.translation: At the meeting, it was agreed that we would watch the film on Saturday.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}で、{土曜日|どようび}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ることになりました。
examples.en: At the meeting, it was agreed that we would watch the film on Saturday.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{店|みせ}を{使|つか}わないことになりました。
examples.en: It has been arranged that we will not use the café tomorrow.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}が{変|か}わって、{私|わたし}が{確認|かくにん}することになりました。
examples.en: After the assignment changed, it was arranged that I would do the check.

grammar.mistake: Both ことにする and ことになる can fit some real decisions. Do not score a context-free choice between them. A rule expressed by ことになっている needs its own established-rule context.

grammar.title: No need is not a prohibition
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + ことはない/ありません. With reassuring context, no need to act. In other contexts, an event does not occur. Past experience たことがない is a different pattern.
grammar.explanation: Use the stated situation to decide what is unnecessary. Bao has already received the requested message, so a duplicate call is not needed. The construction does not ban calls or prove that an action has never happened. Keep the grounds for reassurance explicit.
grammar.example: 連絡はもう届きました。同じ内容で電話することはありません。
grammar.translation: The message has arrived. There is no need to phone with the same information.

examples.ja: {連絡|れんらく}はもう{届|とど}きました。{同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で{電話|でんわ}することはありません。
examples.en: The message has arrived. There is no need to phone with the same information.

examples.ja: {期限|きげん}は{明日|あした}です。{今|いま}、{焦|あせ}ることはありません。
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow. There is no need to rush anxiously now.

examples.ja: この{週|しゅう}の{会議|かいぎ}は{店|みせ}で{開|ひら}きます。{大学|だいがく}で{会|あ}うことはありません。
examples.en: This week’s meeting is held at the café. We will not be meeting at the university.

grammar.mistake: Dictionary + ことはない here is not past + ことがない (“have never”). No need to call is not “you must not call”; context can instead describe no occasions of meeting.

grammar.title: Recognise firm advice from a requested mentor
grammar.formation: Dictionary or ない verb + ことだ/です for advisory use. The speaker takes an authoritative stance. Not every clause + ことです is advice; it may simply identify an action.
grammar.explanation: After Bao asks how to handle the work, the manager can advise dividing tasks and not taking everything on alone. This is firmer than a casual suggestion. Recognise it in the stated relationship; do not turn it into a general request directed at a supervisor. Publisher level tags disagree N3/N2, so later advice practice retrieves it.
grammar.example: 一人で全部引き受けないことです。
grammar.translation: You should not take everything on alone.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{引|ひ}き{受|う}けないことです。
examples.en: You should not take everything on alone.

examples.ja: まず、{仕事|しごと}を{分担|ぶんたん}することです。
examples.en: First, you should divide the work.

examples.ja: {理由|りゆう}が{分|わ}からないときは、{確認|かくにん}することです。
examples.en: When you do not understand the reason, you should check.

grammar.mistake: Negative advice uses verb ない + ことです, not dictionary + ことではありません. For a polite request to a manager, use a request form rather than ordering them with ことだ.

dialogues.title: A café plan and Bao’s choice
dialogues.scene: Bao, Kenta and manager Yamamoto meet at the café about showing their student film. A permitted Saturday arrangement is separate from Bao’s future subtitle check. Kenta’s registration work is not yet done.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {今日|きょう}の{議題|ぎだい}は、{店|みせ}で{映画|えいが}を{見|み}る{会|かい}です。{許可|きょか}は{取|と}りました。
lines.romaji: Kyō no gidai wa, mise de eiga o miru kai desu. Kyoka wa torimashita.
lines.meaning: Today’s agenda item is the film gathering at the café. Permission has been obtained.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {会議|かいぎ}では、{土曜日|どようび}の{三時|さんじ}に{開|ひら}くことで{合意|ごうい}しました。
lines.romaji: Kaigi de wa, doyōbi no sanji ni hiraku koto de gōi shimashita.
lines.meaning: At the meeting, we agreed to hold it on Saturday at three.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{土曜日|どようび}の{三時|さんじ}に、{店|みせ}で{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ることになりました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Doyōbi no sanji ni, mise de eiga o miru koto ni narimashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. It has been arranged that we will watch the film at the café on Saturday at three.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {字幕|じまく}の{方針|ほうしん}は、{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べるようにすることですね。
lines.romaji: Jimaku no hōshin wa, miru hito ga eraberu yō ni suru koto desu ne.
lines.meaning: The subtitle policy is to let viewers choose, right?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: その{方針|ほうしん}です。{仕事|しごと}の{分担|ぶんたん}を{確認|かくにん}しましょう。
lines.romaji: Sono hōshin desu. Shigoto no buntan o kakunin shimashō.
lines.meaning: That is the policy. Let us confirm who handles which tasks.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Watashi wa jimaku no kakunin o hikiukemasu. Kon’ya, futatsu no gamen de kuraberu koto ni shimashita.
lines.meaning: I will take on the subtitle check. I decided to compare it on two screens tonight.

lines.speaker: Kenta

lines.romaji: Onaji jōken de kuraberu n da ne. Kakunin wa mō owatta?
lines.meaning: You will compare under the same conditions, right? Is the check already finished?

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Mada da yo. Kimeta dake de, kakunin wa kon’ya suru. Konkyo mo memo suru yo.
lines.meaning: Not yet. I have only decided; I will check tonight. I will note the grounds too.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {俺|おれ}は{申|もう}し{込|こ}みの{受付|うけつけ}を{担当|たんとう}する。{期限|きげん}は{金曜日|きんようび}だね。
lines.romaji: Ore wa mōshikomi no uketsuke o tantō suru. Kigen wa kin’yōbi da ne.
lines.meaning: I will handle registration. The deadline is Friday, right?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{期限|きげん}と{分担|ぶんたん}を{記録|きろく}して、{慎重|しんちょう}に{準備|じゅんび}しましょう。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kigen to buntan o kiroku shite, shinchō ni junbi shimashō.
lines.meaning: Yes. Let us record the deadline and responsibilities and prepare carefully.

dialogues.title: A duplicate call and shared work
dialogues.scene: The next morning Bao has completed the subtitle comparison. A reply from the manager already confirms the deadline. Bao asks for procedural advice, and Yamamoto recommends sharing the remaining work.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {昨夜|さくや}、{同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}で{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比較|ひかく}しました。{字幕|じまく}の{評価|ひょうか}と{根拠|こんきょ}も{保存|ほぞん}しました。
lines.romaji: Sakuya, onaji jōken de futatsu no gamen o hikaku shimashita. Jimaku no hyōka to konkyo mo hozon shimashita.
lines.meaning: Last night I compared the two screens under the same conditions. I also saved the subtitle assessment and its grounds.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: ありがとう。{決定|けってい}も、{実行|じっこう}したことも{記録|きろく}できましたね。
lines.romaji: Arigatō. Kettei mo, jikkō shita koto mo kiroku dekimashita ne.
lines.meaning: Thank you. You recorded both the decision and what you put into action.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {店長|てんちょう}に{期限|きげん}を{確認|かくにん}するメールを{送|おく}りました。{返事|へんじ}はもう{届|とど}きました。
lines.romaji: Tenchō ni kigen o kakunin suru mēru o okurimashita. Henji wa mō todokimashita.
lines.meaning: I emailed the manager to confirm the deadline. The reply has already arrived.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で{電話|でんわ}することはありません。{返事|へんじ}を{保存|ほぞん}してください。
lines.romaji: Onaji naiyō de denwa suru koto wa arimasen. Henji o hozon shite kudasai.
lines.meaning: There is no need to phone with the same information. Please save the reply.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分|わ}かりました。{準備|じゅんび}が{多|おお}いので、{焦|あせ}っています。どう{進|すす}めたらいいですか？
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Junbi ga ōi no de, asette imasu. Dō susumetara ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: Understood. There is a lot to prepare, so I feel pressed. How should I proceed?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: まず、{仕事|しごと}を{分担|ぶんたん}することです。{一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{引|ひ}き{受|う}けないことです。
lines.romaji: Mazu, shigoto o buntan suru koto desu. Hitori de zenbu hikiukenai koto desu.
lines.meaning: First, you should divide the work. You should not take everything on alone.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。ケンタは{受付|うけつけ}を{担当|たんとう}します。{私|わたし}は{字幕|じまく}の{見直|みなお}しをします。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kenta wa uketsuke o tantō shimasu. Watashi wa jimaku no minaoshi o shimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. Kenta handles registration. I will review the subtitles.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {余分|よぶん}な{作業|さぎょう}も{減|へ}らしましょう。{同|おな}じメモを{二枚|にまい}{印刷|いんさつ}することはありません。
lines.romaji: Yobun na sagyō mo herashimashō. Onaji memo o nimai insatsu suru koto wa arimasen.
lines.meaning: Let us reduce extra work too. There is no need to print the same note twice.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {責任|せきにん}を{確認|かくにん}して、{方針|ほうしん}を{慎重|しんちょう}に{見直|みなお}します。
lines.romaji: Sekinin o kakunin shite, hōshin o shinchō ni minaoshimasu.
lines.meaning: I will confirm the responsibilities and review the policy carefully.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{金曜日|きんようび}の{期限|きげん}は{変|か}わりません。{今日|きょう}は{二人|ふたり}で{準備|じゅんび}を{進|すす}めましょう。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kin’yōbi no kigen wa kawarimasen. Kyō wa futari de junbi o susumemashō.
lines.meaning: Yes. The Friday deadline is unchanged. Let us have the two of you move the preparation forward today.

readings.title: Decided yesterday; carried out last night
paragraphs: {店長|てんちょう}の{許可|きょか}を{取|と}り、{土曜日|どようび}の{三時|さんじ}に{店|みせ}で{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ることになった。{字幕|じまく}は{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べる{方針|ほうしん}だ。{私|わたし}は、{今夜|こんや}{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比較|ひかく}することにした。{会議|かいぎ}では{決|き}めただけで、まだ{確認|かくにん}していなかった。{申|もう}し{込|こ}みの{受付|うけつけ}はケンタが{担当|たんとう}し、{期限|きげん}は{金曜日|きんようび}だ。

{翌朝|よくあさ}、{比較|ひかく}した{結果|けっか}と{根拠|こんきょ}を{報告|ほうこく}した。{店長|てんちょう}からの{返事|へんじ}も{届|とど}いたので、{同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で{電話|でんわ}することはない。{準備|じゅんび}について{相談|そうだん}すると、まず{分担|ぶんたん}することだと{助言|じょげん}された。{一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{引|ひ}き{受|う}けない。{余分|よぶん}な{作業|さぎょう}を{減|へ}らし、{二人|ふたり}で{責任|せきにん}を{確認|かくにん}しながら{進|すす}める。

exercises.prompt: When and where will the gathering take place?
options: Saturday at three, at the café
Friday at midnight, at the university
exercises.explain: The meeting explicitly agrees Saturday at three and Yamamoto confirms the café arrangement.

exercises.prompt: At the meeting, is Bao’s subtitle comparison complete?
options: No; Bao has decided and will check tonight
Yes; Bao finished before the meeting
Yes; Kenta has already checked both screens
exercises.explain: Bao says まだだよ and contrasts the decision with 今夜する.
Kenta explicitly takes registration and confirms Friday as its deadline.

exercises.context: Form practice: express an explicit decision not to rely only on memory. Put ない before ことにしました.
exercises.line: {記憶|きおく}だけに＿＿ことにしました。
exercises.explain: Negative 頼らない precedes こと; the chosen action is not to rely on memory alone.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named arrangement 使わないことになりました with the plain negative verb.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}は{店|みせ}を＿＿ことになりました。
exercises.explain: Use the plain negative before nominalising こと, not a polite finite form.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Kenta: the comparison is still pending and you will do it tonight.
exercises.line: {確認|かくにん}はもう{終|お}わった？
options: まだだよ。{今夜|こんや}、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}で{字幕|じまく}を{確認|かくにん}する。
うん、{昨日|きのう}{全部|ぜんぶ}{終|お}わったよ。
うん、{店|みせ}の{会|かい}はもう{中止|ちゅうし}になったよ。
exercises.explain: Only the first preserves the pending check. The other replies invent completion or cancellation.

exercises.meaning: I decided to check the subtitles tonight.
exercises.explain: The past decision ending does not move the planned 今夜 action into the past.

exercises.prompt: Why is a duplicate phone call unnecessary?
options: The reply has already arrived with the same information
Bao has never used a phone
exercises.explain: Bao says the reply arrived; Yamamoto refers to calling with 同じ内容.

exercises.prompt: What advice does Yamamoto give after Bao asks how to proceed?
options: Divide the work and do not take everything on alone
Delay the gathering until next year
exercises.explain: The two consecutive ことです advice clauses state the division and the negative recommendation.

options: Yes; it is now next month
exercises.explain: The last line explicitly says Friday’s deadline does not change.

exercises.context: Form practice: use dictionary verb + ことはありません for no need to phone; this is not a past-experience sentence.
exercises.line: {同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で＿＿ことはありません。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 電話する completes the requested no-need construction.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete negative advice 引き受けないことです with ない before こと.
exercises.line: {一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}＿＿ことです。
exercises.explain: Negative advice uses the plain negative; it is not a polite finite verb before こと.

exercises.context: Reply politely to your manager: accept shared responsibilities, with Kenta handling registration and you reviewing subtitles.
exercises.line: まず、{仕事|しごと}を{分担|ぶんたん}することです。
options: はい。ケンタは{受付|うけつけ}を{担当|たんとう}し、{私|わたし}は{字幕|じまく}を{見直|みなお}します。
はい。{私|わたし}が{全部|ぜんぶ}{一人|ひとり}でします。
はい。{映画|えいが}はもう{昨年|さくねん}{見|み}ました。
exercises.explain: Only the first accepts the proposed division; the others reject it or change the topic.

exercises.meaning: We will reduce extra work after confirming responsibilities.
tiles: {余分|よぶん}な{作業|さぎょう}を
exercises.explain: Checking the division precedes the reduction; this is a future action, not reported completion.

options: Decision at the meeting → screen check at night → report the next morning
Completed check → meeting next year → no report
Phone ban → canceled gathering → discarded record
exercises.explain: 今夜 at the meeting and 翌朝 with 比較した結果 establish the sequence.
exercises.context: Track relative time and the completed report.

exercises.prompt: Who handles registration, and what is its deadline?
exercises.explain: 申し込みの受付はケンタが担当し、期限は金曜日 explicitly states both.
exercises.context: Do not confuse the registration deadline with the gathering time.

exercises.prompt: What will the remaining preparation look like?
options: Two people share responsibilities and reduce extra work
The group permanently bans phone calls
exercises.explain: The last two sentences state shared responsibilities, reduced extra work and two people proceeding together.
exercises.context: Read the forward plan, not an invented completed event.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a decision or reassuring line from your own clip. Record who chose, whether the action has happened and what gives the speaker grounds. Recognition is not completion or proficiency.
